# WebWell

> WebWell is a free browser extension for Google Chrome and Brave. It replaces the new tab page with a calm dashboard (clock, a daily focus, tasks, landmark photos and music), adds focus sessions with a timer and sound, can block distracting or adult sites when the user turns that on, and tracks screen time privately on the user's own device. No account, no ads, no tracking, open source (MIT).

WebWell is available on the Chrome Web Store (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/webwell/mnjakeggjhfdookcdgjdgmamhcobnofi). It can also be installed from source on GitHub with "Load unpacked" in chrome://extensions or brave://extensions.

Key facts:
- Price: free. There is no paid plan, trial or account.
- Privacy: browsing statistics are stored only in the browser's local storage on the user's device. Nothing is sent to a WebWell server.
- Browsers: Google Chrome and Brave on desktop. Other Chromium browsers may work but are not officially supported. Firefox and Safari are not supported.
- Maker: Adnan, an independent developer. Contact: info.adnanak@gmail.com

## Product

- [WebWell home page](https://webwell.app/): what WebWell does, with a 45-second video tour and screenshots.
- [Frequently asked questions](https://webwell.app/#faq): installation, privacy, blocking, music, supported browsers and offline use.
- [Features: new tab](https://webwell.app/#newtab): clock, daily focus, tasks, quick links and landmark photos that change daily.
- [Features: music](https://webwell.app/#music): Spotify (official embed), SoundCloud, offline rain, noise and wave sounds, lofi radio, and saved songs.
- [Features: focus sessions](https://webwell.app/#focus): a full-screen timer with calming sound; distracting sites are blocked until the session ends.
- [Features: Protect](https://webwell.app/#protect): adult-content filter, short-video blocker, custom block list, mindful pause and parent PIN. All off until the user switches them on.

## Get it

- [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/webwell/mnjakeggjhfdookcdgjdgmamhcobnofi): add WebWell to Chrome or Brave in one click.
- [Install guide](https://webwell.app/install): how to install WebWell from the store, or from source on GitHub.

## Trust and privacy

- [Privacy policy](https://webwell.app/privacy): exactly what the extension stores on the device, when anything leaves the browser, why each permission is needed, and what this website collects.
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/Adnan705/webwell): the full open-source project (MIT licence), including the README and install guide.

## Blog

- [Free Momentum Alternatives for a Calmer New Tab (2026)](https://webwell.app/blog/momentum-alternatives): An honest look at free new-tab extensions like Bonjourr, Tabliss, start.me and WebWell: what each does well, and how to pick one that respects your privacy.
- [How to Block YouTube Shorts on Desktop (Chrome and Brave)](https://webwell.app/blog/block-youtube-shorts-desktop): Three ways to hide or block YouTube Shorts in Chrome and Brave on your computer, from YouTube’s own setting to extensions, with what each one really does.
- [Track Screen Time on Chrome (Free & Private)](https://webwell.app/blog/track-screen-time-chrome-privately): Chrome has no built-in screen time on desktop. Track time per website for free with a private extension: no account, data stays on your device. Here is how.
- [Pomodoro Timer in Chrome: How to Set One Up (and Make It Work)](https://webwell.app/blog/pomodoro-timer-chrome): What the 25/5 rule really is, three ways to run a Pomodoro in Chrome or Brave, and why blocking distractions matters more than the timer.
- [What Permissions Do New Tab and Focus Extensions Really Ask For? (Data Study)](https://webwell.app/blog/extension-permissions-study): A dataset and infographic from the public manifests of seven open-source extensions, plus how to audit any extension.
